contract: DirtyList describes actual content-package coverage, omissions and limits without implying all editor state is clean. Listing must not load or mutate assets.
Explicit save targets only named packages; report partial failures and unknown disk outcomes honestly. Do not imply compile or reload verification. Preserve unrelated assets.
Both save paths exercise owned Blueprint fixtures; widget saves retain thumbnail avoidance. Verify on-disk readback independently, not dirty flag alone.

Undo supports the latest eligible Blueprint transaction only. Preview does not mutate. Missing/stale confirmation, wrong asset, non-TurboMCP transaction, cross-package transaction and active play/transaction refuse. Successful undo restores intended values and leaves unrelated assets unchanged; disk is not reverted.
Review all five tools and shared helpers for behavior, code, comments, clear English output and complete live parameter help.
Reuse existing supporting-tool evidence. Do not increase unique coverage before all five review aspects have evidence. Preserve failures and limitations.
test_scenario: Create two owned assets. Edit the target in a named transaction, list dirty content, preview/refuse/confirm undo, then edit and explicitly save through each path. Independently reload/read back the saved target. Keep an unrelated dirty control unchanged in memory and on disk. Exercise invalid/mixed targets and exact undo boundary controls. Use the serialized runner and restore fixtures.
investigation_findings: DirtyList zero-result wording overstates GetDirtyContentPackages coverage.
Save contains obsolete/unreachable Widget thumbnail guidance and historical comments; reconcile with current direct Widget save path.
Check unloaded target handling, transaction identity/replay and transient cross-object effects before accepting behavior.
